steps.what: List stored interface and data fields
Create prototypes that include the logical model
Add the physical model the record omits

outputs: filed copy of signed prototype note v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored interface and data fields in {CMS}. The developer creates the prototypes, including the logical model, and adds the physical model. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}. The job does not invent the prototype.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fields were copied before each prototype.
tasks.enabler_now: Field identifier and model kind are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The prototype is still made by the developer.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the prototype, not on listing fields.

evidence.claim: Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.

assumptions: Field identifier, model kind, and page identifier are stored on the content record. The content record produces them. A blank kind stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the content record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining creation time is still the developer creating the prototype.

incremental.description: Refresh field identifier and model kind when the content layout changes, and drop a prototype the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many model kinds are blank. The high end assumes field identifier and model kind are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Draft the specification from those rows

loop.purpose: Draft the specification so each sentence cites a stored feature row.
loop.input: Stored specification rows and the outline note.
loop.output: A specification draft whose claims restate those rows.
loop.check: Every number matches a stored row, and every claim is a restatement of that row.
loop.stop: Stop when a number or a claim has no row.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed specification template cannot tell which stored feature identifier the sentence cites.

steps.what: Check each claim restates a feature row

outputs: filed copy of signed specification v1

tasks.design: A job assembles stored specification fields in {DOCS}, including features, protocols, languages, and hardware. The developer outlines the description. A bounded draft writes it only from those rows. The developer checks each claim. A later job files the signed specification in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specification fields were pasted into a fresh description each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Feature identifier and value are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: A claim with no row is still the developer's to reject.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides whether the sentence matches the row.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week checking the description, not on assembling fields.

evidence.claim: Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in 45 percent of tests. Generated code is not treated as safe.

assumptions: Feature identifier, value, protocol, language, and hardware field are stored on the document record. The document record produces them. A blank value stays blank and cannot be cited.
Native configuration of the document record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The draft stops when a claim has no row. It does not invent a feature.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining check time is still the developer checking each claim.

incremental.description: Refresh feature identifier and value when the document layout changes, and drop a specification the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many feature values are blank. The high end assumes feature identifier and value are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Evaluate the server hardware and software
Recommend what to keep or replace

outputs: filed copy of signed hardware recommendation v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored server capacity in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The developer evaluates the hardware or software and recommends what to keep or replace. A later job files the signed recommendation in {DOCS}. It does not buy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity figures were copied before each recommendation.
tasks.enabler_now: Server identifier, metric, and value are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The recommendation is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides what to recommend.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the recommendation, not on listing capacity.

reach.task: Order only after a separate signature

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a pipeline tests and scans every change, work stays on a branch, and a person merges.

assumptions: Server identifier, metric, and value are stored on the operations record. The operations record produces them. A blank value stays blank and is not treated as zero.
Native configuration of the operations record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
Filing the recommendation does not place an order.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining evaluation time is still the developer evaluating the hardware.

incremental.description: Refresh server identifier, metric, and value when the operations layout changes, and drop a recommendation the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many capacity values are blank. The high end assumes server identifier, metric, and value are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor and identify problems in the alerts
Notify the security specialist of the problem
Send only the signed specialist notice
outputs: filed copy of signed specialist notice v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored security alerts in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The developer monitors them, identifies the problem, and writes the notice. A later job sends only that signed notice by {EMAIL}. The job does not watch named staff, does not rate staff, and does not file a statutory incident report. It does not treat the firm as in scope.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alerts were copied into a message by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Alert identifier, time, and message are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The developer still decides whether it is a problem.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides what the specialist is told.

ambition.what: Notify the specialist the day the alert is stored.

tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the problem, not on collecting alerts.

reach.task: Act only on the signed notice

evidence.claim: Digest [S22] says logging is limited to what is strictly necessary and proportionate.
Digest [S23] says works-council consent is required before logs or a dashboard observe staff.
Digest [S16] says a Dutch cyber duty applies from 15 August 2026. This design does not treat the firm as in scope.
Digest [S19] says an incident report is due at 24 hours, 72 hours, and one month. This design does not send that report.
Digest [S24] says rating staff is a high-risk use. This design does not rate staff.
Digest [S25] says that high-risk duty applies from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Alert identifier, time, and message are stored on the operations record. The operations record produces them. A blank message stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the operations record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The list is alert rows, not a dashboard of named staff. Consent to observe staff is a separate decision, and this design does not ask for it.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining monitoring time is still the developer identifying the problem.

incremental.description: Refresh alert identifier, time, and message when the operations layout changes, and drop a notice the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many alert messages are blank. The high end assumes alert identifier, time, and message are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The web developer spends the week writing, reviewing, and merging. A stored failing check, a blank field, and filing a signed note can move. The developer still reviews every change, and no job changes a live system alone.
reach: A reviewer reads the change before the developer merges it.
A specialist receives only the notice the developer signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a list that is missing a stored field.
Reject a sentence that does not restate a stored row.
Reject a live change that is not the signed set.
role.ambitious_version: A signed change can be filed the same week, and the developer still owns the merge.
